summary: The original is a sparse, permanently-busy field of red-to-magenta comets streaking both ways along the strip; the port paints comet trails that never decay, so it fills to a solid full-magenta strip within ~2 s and stays frozen there indefinitely.
observations: Neither side exposes any controls (meta.json sides.orig.controls and sides.port.controls are both empty; --probe-controls printed '(no settable controls)' for both). Control surfaces therefore match.
Neither side binds sensors (wantsSensors false on both, sensors 'off'). Rig is the default 60-px strip.

ORIGINAL, steady state (30-40 s window, --label late, 20 fps): a continuously replenished field of ~10-15 short comets. Each comet is a 5-9 px triangular trail with a bright head and a geometric fade behind it — --dump at t=30 s shows e.g. head 15:(255,0,18) then 16:(122,0,8) 17:(50,0,3) 18:(15,0,1) 19:(3,0,0), with a mirrored ramp on the leading side. About 23-36 of 60 pixels are lit at any instant; the rest are exactly (0,0,0). Mean brightness holds steady around 16-18 across every window and every seed tried.

ORIGINAL motion: comets travel at roughly 1 px/frame at 20 fps (~20 px/s). --dump at 30 / 30.15 / 30.3 s tracks heads 15 -> 12 -> 9, 34 -> 32 -> 29, 55 -> 52 -> 50, i.e. leftward. The baseline and seed waterfalls show streaks slanting BOTH ways with a spread of slopes, so comets run in both directions at somewhat varied speeds, crossing each other constantly. Motion stat avg 17-28 across all runs; zeroMotionFrames 4/120 in baseline.

ORIGINAL colour: red-blue only, meanG is exactly 0 in every window. Heads span deep red (255,0,18) through magenta (255,0,163) — different comets carry different amounts of blue, but none reach full magenta.

PORT, steady state (30-40 s, --label late): completely static. --dump at 30 / 30.15 / 30.3 s returns 59 of 60 pixels at exactly (255,0,255) at all three times; only pixel 0 flickers (0,0,0) <-> (41,0,0). motion avg 0, zeroMotionFrames 77/120 in the 6 s baseline and effectively total in the late window. The 60 s survey waterfall is one unbroken magenta block after the first ~2 s.

PORT, opening transient: the trails do exist briefly but they never erase. --dump on --label dump-early counts full-magenta pixels 0 -> 11 -> 45 -> 59 -> 59 -> 59 at t = 0.05 / 0.5 / 1 / 2 / 4 / 7.9 s, and the t=0.5 s frame shows two solid magenta blocks growing inward from pixels 1-6 and 53-59 with a partial-brightness pixel (181,0,115) at each advancing edge. So the port draws comet-like heads with a fade at the front edge, but every pixel a head has passed is latched at full brightness forever. The whole strip is saturated by ~t=2 s.

PORT brightness is ~9x the original's: meanBrightness avg 146 (baseline) / 162 (survey) / 167 (late) against the original's 17-18. Both sides have meanG exactly 0, so the port is at least in the right hue family (red/magenta), but it sits pinned at the extreme magenta end (255,0,255) that the original never reaches.

Seed-independent: seeds 1, 7 and 1234 (20 s @ 10 fps) all show the same picture — original mean 15-18 / motion 23-28 with a dense crossing-comet waterfall, port mean 159-162 / motion 1 with a solid magenta block. The divergence is not a one-seed fluke.
The first ~0.5 s is the only stretch where the two sides are comparable: both start black and both light a similar handful of pixels (orig 17, port 14 lit at t=0.5 s). Everything after that diverges.
feedback: The port's core bug is that pixel state is never cleared or decayed between frames. Whatever a comet head lights stays lit at full brightness permanently, so the strip monotonically fills and is 100% saturated magenta by t~2 s and dead-static from then on. Every frame must start from a cleared strip (or from an explicitly decayed one), so that only the current comets and their trails are lit.

Target steady state on a 60-px strip: ~10-15 comets alive at once, ~23-36 of 60 pixels lit at any instant, the rest exactly (0,0,0), and mean strip brightness holding near 17 indefinitely. The port currently posts mean 167 with ~59/60 lit.

Trail shape to aim for: a bright head with a roughly geometric falloff over 4 px on each side — measured values on the original are head 255, then 122, 50, 15, 3. The port's trail edge shows only a single intermediate pixel (~181) before jumping to full, so the falloff is far too short as well as non-clearing.

Motion to aim for: ~1 px per frame at 20 fps (~20 px/s), with comets travelling in BOTH directions and a spread of speeds so streaks cross each other. The original's waterfall is a lattice of opposing diagonals; the port's transient fills inward from both ends only, so it may be spawning only at the two strip ends rather than at random positions.

Colour range is too narrow and too hot: the original's comet heads vary from (255,0,18) deep red to about (255,0,163) magenta — per-comet variation in the blue channel, green always 0. The port emits a single uniform (255,0,255), i.e. maximum blue on every comet. Give each comet its own red-to-magenta hue and keep it short of full magenta.

Comets must keep spawning forever — the original's density and mean brightness are unchanged from t=0 to t=40 s. Verify any fix over at least a 30-60 s window, not the first few seconds: the port's opening 0.5 s already looks roughly right today and only the long window exposes the failure.
